hypothesis: Honoring each production HIP-3 signal frame's long_exit and short_exit columns while retaining the deployed fixed 80-bps stop and 24-hour maximum hold will improve validation economics relative to ignoring those exits.
decision: Reject direct signal-exit execution for v26. The bounded challenger increased turnover and materially degraded both Swing routes under nominal and stress friction. It also degraded index Breakout; commodity Breakout was economically unchanged under stress and slightly worse by profit factor. Preserve the current fixed-stop, opposite-intent, and maximum-hold lifecycle while continuing to record signal exits as report-only challenger evidence. Do not alter the running backend or staged v26 execution contract from this result.
falsifier: Update this rejection if a combined-priority shared-account replay or a sufficient reconciled live sample shows signal-exit execution improving after-cost profit factor and drawdown without unacceptable churn across both development and forward windows. One isolated avoided loss is insufficient.
limitations: The experiment is a single-provider independent-asset 15-minute approximation, not combined live portfolio parity.
The configured Swing recipes use alignment-loss exits for index assets and HA-flip exits for commodity assets; the experiment does not optimize new exit thresholds.
The sealed holdout was not inspected, preserving it for later confirmation.
This rejection applies to direct signal-exit execution, not every possible profit-lock or lifecycle adaptation.
No live position, order, route, sizing rule, or execution authority changed.
